name: Glycogenolysis
summary: Fasting (glucagon, liver) and exercise (epinephrine, AMP, Ca²⁺ in muscle). Glycogen phosphorylase (rate-limiting, needs B6) cleaves α-1,4 bonds with Pi to release glucose-1-phosphate until 4 residues from a branch (limit dextrin); debranching enzyme moves 3 of them and frees the last as glucose. Liver uses glucose-6-phosphatase to export glucose; muscle keeps G6P for glycolysis. Glycogen storage diseases: von Gierke (I, glucose-6-phosphatase), Pompe (II, lysosomal acid α-glucosidase), Cori (III, debranching enzyme), Andersen (IV, branching enzyme), McArdle (V, muscle phosphorylase), Hers (VI, liver phosphorylase).

glycogen.name: Glycogen
glycogen.notes: Pompe disease (GSD II): lysosomal acid α-glucosidase (acid maltase) deficiency — glycogen builds up in lysosomes; cardiomegaly, hypotonia, early death in the infantile form. Not part of the cytosolic pathway.

limit.name: Limit dextrin
limit.notes: Glycogen trimmed to 4 residues from each branch point — phosphorylase can go no closer. Accumulates in Cori disease.

g6p.name: Glucose-6-phosphate
g6p.notes: Muscle sends it into glycolysis (no glucose-6-phosphatase).

glucose.name: Glucose
glucose.notes: Made in the ER lumen by glucose-6-phosphatase (liver and kidney) and exported to the blood. Muscle lacks this enzyme, so its glycogen only feeds its own glycolysis.

glucosec.name: Glucose (cytosol)
glucosec.notes: About 8–10% of the glucose from glycogen: the debranching enzyme frees each α-1,6 branch point as glucose, not G1P.

gp.name: Glycogen phosphorylase
gp.notes: Rate-limiting; needs pyridoxal phosphate (B6). Activated by phosphorylation (phosphorylase kinase ← PKA; glucagon, epinephrine), AMP and Ca²⁺ (muscle); inhibited by insulin, ATP, G6P and glucose (liver). McArdle disease (GSD V) = muscle isoform (myophosphorylase): exercise cramps, myoglobinuria, no lactate rise, second-wind phenomenon. Hers disease (GSD VI) = liver isoform: mild fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly.

gde.name: Debranching enzyme
gde.notes: Two activities: 4-α-glucanotransferase moves 3 residues to another chain, then α-1,6-glucosidase releases the branch residue as free glucose. Deficiency = Cori disease (GSD III): like a milder von Gierke with normal lactate; limit dextrin–like structures accumulate.

g6pase.name: Glucose-6-phosphatase
g6pase.notes: ER lumen of liver and kidney, not muscle. Deficiency = von Gierke disease (GSD I): severe fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, hepatomegaly, hyperuricemia, hypertriglyceridemia, doll-like face.
